questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Is he not driving a car?

options.text: Was he not driving a car?
Is a car not being driven by him?
Is a car not been driven by him?
Does he not drive a car?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is:** Is a car not being driven by him?**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **subject** of the **Active Voice** is changed into the **object** of the **Passive Voice**. Also, the **object** of the **Active Voice** is changed into the **subject **of the **Passive Voice**.
 
• The usage of a **helping verb** is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.
 
• The preposition** “by” **is used before the object made in Passive Voice. However, it is optional in some cases.
 
• The Active voice in this question is in **Present Continuous**. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in **Present Continuous**.
 
• The format of Active voice is: **Am/is/are + Subject + Verb (ing) + Object.**
 
• Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: **Am/is/are + Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + being + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).**

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Is a car not being driven by him?**

questions.solution:

__
 
• The sentence *"Radium is a white powder that ________ table salt."* is in **present tense.**
 
• **This infers** that we need a verb that also aligns with the present tense, while also agreeing with the singular noun **"Radium"**.
 
• **"Looks like"** is the correct answer because it agrees with the singular subject "Radium" and is in the present tense.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is- *"Radium is a white powder that** looks like **table salt".*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png]

• Option 3 **"will look like"** implies a future tense, which is inconsistent with the present tense structure of the sentence.
 
• Option 4** "looking like"** is in the present continuous tense and doesn't fit in the structure of the sentence.

Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

They are the people __which are looking to expand__ their horizons in the fast growing tourism industry.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 3' **i.e.** 'who are looking to expand'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **sentence is referring** to the group of people who have a certain aim to expand their horizons in the tourism industry. In English grammar, when** referring to** **people**, we use** 'who'** not '**which'.**
 
• The error in the sentence lies in the usage of the relative pronoun 'which' for referring to people. The correct relative pronoun to use for people is 'who'.
 
• The verb form **'are looking to expand'** correctly maintains agreement with the plural subject (the people).

Therefore, the** corrected sentence** should be "*They are the people **who are looking to expand** their horizons in the fast growing tourism industry."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **'which looked to expand' is incorrect because 'which' is not the correct relative pronoun to refer to people. Also, the use of past tense 'looked' is not consistent with the other verbs of the sentence that are in the present tense.
 
• **Option 2: **'who is looking to expand' is grammatically incorrect. 'Is looking' would be incorrect verb agreement for the plural subject 'people'.
 
• **Option 4:** 'that are looked to expand' is grammatically incorrect. The verb phrase 'are looked to expand' doesn't make sense in the context of the sentence.

questions.question: Describe how you will tell your teacher that the windmill is being built by Master Yadav In active voice.

options.text: The windmill is be built by Master Yadav.
Master Yadav been building the windmill.
Master Yadav is building the windmill.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** "Master Yadav is building the windmill."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is in active voice, which means the subject (Master Yadav) is performing the action (building the windmill).
 
• The correct tense to use here is present continuous (is building) because the action is currently happening.
 
• The sentence is grammatically correct and conveys the intended meaning clearly

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1: This sentence is in passive voice, which means the subject (windmill) is receiving the action (being built). It is grammatically correct but does not convey the information about who is building the windmill.
 
• Option 2: This sentence is in present perfect continuous tense (has/have been building), which indicates a continuous action that started in the past and is still ongoing. However, it does not convey the information about who is building the windmill.
 
• Option 3: This sentence is in simple present tense (build), which is grammatically correct but does not convey the information about the ongoing action.

Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

B. Many companies use it for executive recruitment and analysis.

C. Despite public scepticism, graphology plays a covert role in British management.

D. Modern graphology began early in the 19th century when French churchman Jean Hippolyte Michon created the first graphological ‘catalogue’.

__
 
• **Sentence D** provides the historical context of modern graphology.
 
• **Sentence C** highlights the public perception of graphology, while also hinting at its covert use in British management.
 
• **Sentence B** explains the practical application of graphology in executive recruitment and analysis.
 
• **Sentence A** further elaborates on the benefits of using graphology in evaluating candidates.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2 (ABCD)**: This arrangement reverses the logical flow of the paragraph, starting with the practical application of graphology before providing historical and contextual information.
 
• **Option 3 (ABDC)**: This arrangement places sentence A before sentence B, which disrupts the logical flow of the paragraph and creates confusion.
 
• **Option 4 (CBDA)**: This arrangement places sentence C at the beginning, which does not provide any context for the reader and makes the paragraph seem disjointed.

• Different colors were used to **dye the strings, with yellow representing money and red standing for battle or warriors.**

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"surface". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Surface refers to the outer or the top layer of something where activities can occur.
 
• With regards to the eye, light must be focused on the surface of the retina, which makes this the most appropriate term to use in this setting.
 
• Therefore, the sentence should read: "It is necessary to focus the scattered light at the retina's surface."
 
 
• The lens and cornea of the eye together focus incoming light onto the surface of the retina, where the light-sensitive cells are stimulated and send signals to the brain to form an image.
 
 

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 4". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "lane" - This word generally refers to a narrow road or a defined path for vehicles or people to travel through.
 
 
• The retina in the eye doesn't have lanes; it's an organ with a surface which receives light, so this option doesn't fit.
